items.area: R1 — in-house service from the Service's own container
items.description: aac-tools generator: resolve a Service's in-house product from its own container, so kube-coder-tunnel-reclaim can be mapped. The generator takes an exposed Service's in-house service from the container the Service routes to, not from every container of the pod. Today that is the union in `_inhouse_service_for`, ArgoCDTools aac-tools/image/gen_architecture.py:1388-1397, called at :1282. KubeCoderDeploy's judgment layer maps `kube-coder-tunnel-reclaim: app:kube-coder-tunnel-reclaim`, replacing the comment at architecture.yaml:21-25. A prd generation with the published generator then prints no `gap:` line for the image, and kubecoder.home still references svc:kubecoder-controller-api with no duplicate service minted. The controller Service lands on the nginx `ingress` sidecar and names the controller through `nginx.webathome.org/target-port: "8080"` (chart/templates/controller-service.yaml).
items.rationale: Generator picks the in-house service from the routed container (gen_architecture.py:1443-1451 uses the exposures identity; test_the_in_house_service_is_the_routed_containers_not_the_pods). KubeCoderDeploy origin/main maps kube-coder-tunnel-reclaim: app:kube-coder-tunnel-reclaim; P5 record: no gap line, no minted service.

items.area: R2 — Argo CD's capability and redis edges (generator)
items.description: aac-tools: Argo CD's model gets no capability and no edges to its redis, because the generator's hooks cannot reach them. The generator now reaches them in two ways. First, a judgment layer can scope an image entry's `realizes`, and its `upstream` wire, to named containers of that image. Today realizes is looked up per image name, gen_architecture.py:934-935, applied at :965 and :1008-1014, and an image-level upstream hard-fails on a container that lacks the var, :1609-1614. Second, an env value sourced through `valueFrom.configMapKeyRef` resolves against the ConfigMap the same render carries. Today env capture keeps literal values only, :977, and ConfigMaps are collected at :1077-1078. Values sourced from a Secret stay unresolved, as today (:629-633). An `upstream` wire still hard-fails on a container it applies to that does not set its variable (Ruling D4).
items.rationale: Container-scoped realizes/upstream and configMapKeyRef resolution present (gen_architecture.py:760-770); tests at test_gen_architecture.py:1296-1420 (scoped realizes, scoped upstream from ConfigMap, unknown container gap, ConfigMap/key absent leaves var unset).

items.area: R2 — Argo CD's capability and redis edges (published model)
items.description: The consequence is gone: "The published model shows Argo CD and its redis side by side with no edge between them, and Argo CD is missing from the Delivery pipeline view." In the published dataset, Argo CD's controllers realize cap:configuration-management, and the copyutil init container and the redis-secret-init Job realize nothing. The redis instance has a Serving edge to each Argo CD container that reads REDIS_SERVER. The Delivery view selects that capability (Architecture views/delivery.yaml:10), which nothing realizes today, and it now shows Argo CD. ArgoCDDeploy's judgment layer maps `argocd: ss:argo-cd` with no realizes today (architecture.yaml:21-26).
items.rationale: Ran `cexec aac-tools gen-architecture --stage prd --producer argocd-deploy` in ArgoCDDeploy: 5 controllers realize cap:configuration-management (copyutil/secret-init none); redis has Serving edges to server, repo-server, application-controller.

items.area: R1/R2/R4 — the generator is published before its consumers
items.description: Every deploy repo was regenerated before ArgoCDTools was pushed: 48 repos and 49 published stages, each with the published generator (origin/main, 8914c0f at planning) and with the new one. Every difference is accounted for as intended, and no repo that generated before fails with the new generator. Before that push, the run's first, no repo the run would push carried unpushed commits that were not this slice's (Ruling F1). items.area: R5 — Alertmanager's dependency on the Telegram Bot API
items.description: Before: "The generated architecture has a svc:telegram-bot-api serving edge for jenkins-telegram-bot … but nothing declares one for Alertmanager, so the model does not show that alert delivery depends on Telegram." PrometheusDeploy's judgment layer now declares svc:telegram-bot-api serving the alertmanager image; today it is bare `alertmanager: ss:alertmanager` (architecture.yaml:19). The id is the composite `svc:telegram-bot-api,6708ef33-aaf7-4acd-a10d-560d7a7e1d48` (Architecture docs/architecture/external-services.yaml:29), because served_by is passed through unresolved (gen_architecture.py:1017). The published model shows a Serving edge from the Telegram Bot API service to Alertmanager. Alertmanager sends through `telegram_configs` (config/prd/values.yaml:353,361).
items.rationale: PrometheusDeploy origin/main architecture.yaml: alertmanager has served_by ["svc:telegram-bot-api,6708ef33-..."] with comment on telegram_configs; P7 record confirms Serving edge.

items.area: R6 — every copied arch-validate.py on the toolchain
items.description: Cross-repo: migrate every copied arch-validate.py to the aac-tools toolchain. No active producer repo carries a copy of arch-validate.py. GitHub's own tree of every non-archived pvginkel repo holds the file only at two paths. One is Architecture's canonical `.claude/architecture/arch-validate.py`. The other is ArgoCDTools' `aac-tools/image/arch-validate.py`, the toolchain image's source (aac-tools/Dockerfile:62 installs it as /usr/local/bin/arch-validate). The archived DesignAssistant and SomfyRemote keep theirs, and so does HelmCharts if slice 029 archived it first (Ruling F1). The carrier set was listed with gitblit's `find_files` `**/arch-validate.py` and confirmed against those GitHub trees (Ruling F2). Every former carrier runs `arch-validate` from the aac-tools toolchain wherever it ran the copy: its architecture Jenkinsfile, its local gate and any instruction naming the script. Each migrated carrier's architecture build is green on its migrated head. Where a carrier's local gate moved onto the toolchain, its KubeCoder environment declares aac-tools.
items.rationale: Only two arch-validate.py remain in the active estate (Architecture canonical, ArgoCDTools image source; scratch review mutants aside). 28 carriers migrated per sweep_ledger, each AaC build green; Ansible migrated in a882eb6 (gates green after rebase).
